content:
Since the debut of the iPhone Duo, the concept of keeping all primary interface navigation elements within the reach of your thumb has been genuinely thrilling. Apple redefined smartphone navigation design with the Duo’s external display, and now seeing other phones stash functions at the top feels oddly out of place.

The nostalgia for smaller phones largely comes from how reachable everything used to be. The trade-off, of course, was a fairly small screen — and content presentation has come a long way since then.

The Duo resolves both issues: a sensibly proportioned rectangular viewing area on the left, with the base and navigation on the right. You get ample viewing real estate, and every control still sits comfortably within thumb’s reach.

Ever since Apple unveiled this design, enthusiasts have floated the idea of an “iPhone Solo” — a non-folding version with the Duo’s screen size.

I don’t expect Apple to ship such a device, but it’s a genuinely interesting thought, and depending on how the Duo lands, it might make sense one day. When you think about it, today’s smartphone aspect ratio is a historical accident. We once used 16:9 displays, then killed every bezel and the Home button, leaving us with oddly tall, awkward-to-hand-hold slabs where too much is out of single-hand reach.

The Duo re-imagines the smartphone form factor. Apple didn’t just port a normal iOS experience onto the outer display — it redesigned from the ground up to make the most of it, and honestly, it makes me envious of a phone where everything is right at your fingertips.

Top comment posted by Joe

The iPhone mini already went a step further than the Duo by fitting everything into thumb’s reach thanks to its width — which is precisely why it won over fans including me.

I’m not convinced the same can be achieved at the Duo’s width and thickness, but I’m still keen to try it in person.

We’ll see what happens next. If the outside display on the Duo is well received, an iPhone Solo could very well become reality.

What do you think of the Solo concept? Would you buy one? Let us know in the comments.
